root_cause.text: In `fs/ntfs3/file.c` (`ntfs_compress_write()`), the write path could repeatedly compute the same `valid` offset for `ni->i_valid` when scanning the `[valid : pos)` range, causing the loop to make no progress and spin indefinitely.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ni->i_valid == valid) { err = -EINVAL; goto out; }` before assigning `ni->i_valid = valid`, and the CVE description says “if the retrieved valid value is always the same, this can trigger a potential infinite loop,” with syzbot reporting `ntfs_file_write_iter()` hanging under `inode_lock`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In `fs/ntfs3/file.c` (`ntfs_compress_write()`), the write path could repeatedly compute the same `valid` offset for `ni->i_valid` when scanning the `[valid : pos)` range, causing the loop to make no progress and spin indefinitely.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (ni->i_valid == valid) { err = -EINVAL; goto out; }` before assigning `ni->i_valid = valid`, and the CVE description says “if the retrieved valid value is always the same, this can trigger a potential infinite loop,” with syzbot reporting `ntfs_file_write_iter()` hanging under `inode_lock`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject unchanged sparse write progress by returning -EINVAL when the computed valid extent does not advance i_valid.
intent_record.what: In the SPARSE_LCN branch of ntfs_compress_write(), the code no longer assigns ni->i_valid and valid in a single statement. Instead, it computes valid first, checks whether ni->i_valid already equals that value, and if so sets err to -EINVAL and exits via out. Only when the value differs does it assign ni->i_valid = valid and continue.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from treating an unchanged sparse extent boundary as a successful progress update. If the computed valid offset matches the current i_valid, the write now fails with -EINVAL instead of silently continuing, avoiding redundant or invalid state progression during compressed sparse writes.

grouping_result.intent: Reject unchanged sparse write progress by returning -EINVAL when the computed valid extent does not advance i_valid.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the same write-path issue in ntfs3 by preventing no-progress scans of the valid extent. Returning -EINVAL when the computed valid extent does not advance i_valid addresses the infinite loop/spin caused by repeatedly computing the same valid offset.

candidates.rationale: This assignment updates i_valid to the computed valid offset, but before the fix it could repeatedly assign the same value during the [valid:pos) scan, causing no forward progress and an infinite loop.

vuln_statements.explanation: This assignment is the statement involved in updating i_valid during the [valid:pos) scan. Before the fix, it could repeatedly compute and reassign the same valid offset without advancing, causing the loop in ntfs_compress_write() to make no progress and spin indefinitely.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function `ntfs_compress_write()` contains the vulnerable write-path loop and the exact progress condition from the root cause. In the loop `while (valid < pos)`, when `attr_data_get_block()` reports a sparse extent it updates `ni->i_valid = valid = frame_vbo + ((u64)clen << sbi->cluster_bits);` and `continue;`. This is the critical construct because it recomputes `valid` from the current frame boundary, and the function later uses `pos`/`valid` to drive progress through `[valid : pos)`. There is no additional guard here preventing repeated computation of the same `valid` offset or ensuring forward progress beyond that assignment. The snippet also lacks any later fix such as advancing `valid` unconditionally past the current frame or breaking on non-progress, so the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet present in this commit.
